item.title: Strategic Communications Manager
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 10/28/2026.

Note: All VDEM employees are designated essential personnel and may be required to work during emergencies, including irregular hours and at locations other than the official duty station. The primary agency spokesperson role requires media interview experience. No visa sponsorship. Fingerprint-based criminal history background check, DMV check, and E-Verify required. 1-year probationary period. Salary $90,000–$95,000. Apply at jobs.virginia.gov.

The Virginia Department of Emergency Management (VDEM) seeks a Strategic Communications Manager to support the Director of Communications in carrying out the objectives of the Communications Division, which protects the lives and property of Virginia’s citizens through effective strategic use of multiple communications platforms, educational outreach initiatives, and training of public information officers. The role manages agency outreach initiatives and communication efforts across all channels (web, mobile, print, digital media), serves as the primary agency spokesperson, and is the point of contact for media relations. Salary $90,000–$95,000.

Key responsibilities include: managing the agency’s outreach initiatives and communication efforts, as well as assisting with creative and content development across all channels; establishing strong working relationships and acting as a central resource across all divisions of the agency; assuring intentional cultural sensitivity and inclusivity in all internal and external communications; leading the routine, time-sensitive, and delegated aspects of agency communications and public relations including implementation of communication deliverables and management of projects; managing internal and external communication structures and timelines including social media, web, internal platforms (SharePoint), and other mediums; serving as the primary agency spokesperson; and serving as the point of contact for media relations.

Qualifications: knowledge of strategic communications, public relations, crisis communications, and media relations principles; knowledge of emergency management operations, incident response frameworks, and Joint Information Center (JIC) functions; skill in media relations, public speaking, and spokesperson preparation; knowledge of digital communication platforms; ability to develop clear, concise, compelling, audience-specific messaging in AP Style; and skill in strategic planning, project management, and coordinating multiple priorities under tight deadlines. Professional experience in public relations or news media conducting media interviews preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary $90,000–$95,000 negotiable within hiring range. Comprehensive Virginia state benefits. Apply at jobs.virginia.gov. No visa sponsorship. All VDEM employees designated as essential personnel.

The Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR) seeks an experienced, highly organized, and analytical professional to serve as Senior Policy Analyst in the Office of Policy, Planning and Legislative Affairs. This position serves as a senior professional resource supporting DCR’s agencywide policy management, legislative coordination, strategic planning, regulatory and guidance activities, and other special policy initiatives. The analyst works with DCR leadership, division subject-matter experts, and other Policy Office staff to research complex issues, review and develop agency policies, evaluate policy options, support legislative activities, and help ensure that important agencywide processes are completed accurately and on schedule. Salary $95,000–$105,000. Richmond, VA.

Key responsibilities include: conducting policy, legislative, statutory, regulatory, and legal-policy research and analysis and developing options and recommendations for management; developing and conducting substantive review of agencywide policies, legislative initiatives, proposed statutory language, amendments, analyses, and executive briefing materials; analyzing statutes, regulations, Executive Orders, and legislative history to identify policy implications, alternatives, risks, and implementation requirements; during General Assembly sessions, analyzing complex legislation and studies, coordinating program input, assessing agency impacts, and preparing recommendations and decision materials for leadership; leading complex cross-divisional policy projects and studies from initial research through final recommendation; working with subject-matter experts, legal counsel, legislative staff, other agencies, and stakeholders to develop practical agency-level policy solutions; and representing DCR on assigned committees, workgroups, studies, and interagency projects.

Qualifications: demonstrated experience conducting policy, legislative, governmental, program, or legal-policy research and analysis; experience reviewing, drafting, or editing policies, procedures, legislation, reports, or other complex professional documents; ability to interpret and apply laws, regulations, policies, procedures, and administrative requirements; strong analytical, writing, editing, and critical-thinking skills; strong organizational and project-coordination skills; and ability to work independently while recognizing when management or legal review is needed. Experience in Virginia state government or with legislative or executive processes preferred; valid driver’s license required.

Compensation and logistics: salary $95,000–$105,000. Comprehensive Virginia state benefits including PSLF eligibility, paid leave, medical/dental/vision, and retirement. Free Virginia State Parks admission. Occasional overnight travel. Richmond, VA. Valid driver’s license required.

item.description:
Application period: October–November 2026. Apply via inspira.un.org. The 2026 application window is now open.

Note: This is a competitive examination program, not a direct hire. Successful candidates are placed on a roster for P-1 or P-2 level positions — placement on the roster does not guarantee an offer of employment. For 2026, the United States is a participating country for the Development and Sustainability exam area only. Must be 32 years of age or younger (born on or after January 1, 1994). Must be willing to serve at any UN duty station worldwide. Attach a government-issued photo ID and degree documentation to your application.

The UN Young Professionals Programme (YPP) is a recruitment initiative for talented professionals to start a career as an international civil servant with the UN Secretariat. The examination process consists of a two-stage online written exam followed by a competency-based video-conference interview. Successful candidates are placed on a roster valid for three years from which they are selected to fill appropriate vacancies at UN offices worldwide (including Addis Ababa, Bangkok, Beirut, Geneva, Nairobi, New York, Santiago, and Vienna). Successful candidates receive a two-year fixed-term contract at the P-1 or P-2 level, with the possibility of a continuing contract after two years subject to satisfactory performance.

Estimated timeline: Application period October–November → Applications screened December–January → Assessment process February–May → Interviews and results June–August. Note: timeline varies year to year.

The YPP exam has two online stages: Stage 1 consists of approximately 2 hours of multiple choice questions (general and specialized), available in English or French. Stage 2 consists of approximately 2–2.5 hours of specialized constructed-response questions; may be proctored remotely. Candidates successful in both stages are invited to a competency-based video-conference interview.

Eligibility requirements: nationality of a participating Member State (U.S. eligible for Development & Sustainability exam area in 2026); a bachelor's degree or equivalent (at least a 3-year degree) relevant to the exam area; 32 years of age or younger in 2026 (born on or after January 1, 1994); fluency in English or French (UN Level II proficiency required in all four areas — speaking, reading, writing, and understanding).

Compensation and logistics: P-1 or P-2 level UN salary scale (competitive international civil service compensation including benefits and allowances — confirm current rates via careers.un.org). 2-year fixed-term contract. Placement at any UN duty station worldwide. Application via inspira.un.org. Application period: October–November 2026.

A fellowship opportunity is available in the Office of Health Policy within the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation (ASPE) at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) in Washington, DC. Note: this is an ORISE-administered fellowship (administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy). Participants do not become employees of HHS, DOE, or the program administrator -- this is a stipend, not a salary, and there are no employment-related benefits. U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency required. A master's or doctoral degree received within the past 5 years is required. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis; final deadline December 1, 2026.

The selected fellow will be mentored by a team of economic, policy, and public health experts who focus on healthcare markets, and will have opportunities to train with a wide range of data resources, collaborate on research studies, and engage in both quantitative and qualitative analytical projects in support of ASPE's priorities. Learning objectives include: developing and maintaining subject matter expertise in rural healthcare systems, Medicaid policy, and Health Insurance Marketplace financing and eligibility frameworks; analyzing regulations, legislation, executive directives, and policy reports; conducting and supporting research and program evaluation activities; synthesizing complex policy information into clear, actionable insights; and drafting professional correspondence, policy briefs, reports, presentations, and talking points.

Qualifications: a master's or doctoral degree in a relevant field (social science or related) received within the past five years; experience designing, planning, conducting, and communicating the results of analytical projects within economics or related fields; and knowledge of and experience with methodological and statistical techniques. The office has particular interest in applicants with experience in demography or actuarial science (not required). U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency required.

Compensation and logistics: monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience; stipend for healthcare benefits (not employer-sponsored benefits). One-year initial appointment, may be renewed contingent on funding. Full-time. Based in Washington, DC. Application deadline: December 1, 2026 (rolling reviews).
